# Documentation Split Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Split the 492-line README into a 30-second README, an authored `docs/manual.md` that is the single source of reference truth, and a `man/mdmost.1` generated by pandoc in CI and never committed.

**Architecture:** `docs/manual.md` becomes the one place every key, option and config field is documented. `man/mdmost.1` stops being a hand-maintained duplicate and becomes a build artifact produced by `make man`; `man/` is gitignored, so it cannot go stale. The README keeps only what sells and installs the pager, and links to the manual by absolute URL because the crate excludes `docs/`. A new terminal-setup section explains the font coverage the renderer needs, and a new test pins the glyph inventory that section claims, so the prose cannot silently stop matching the renderer.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024, pandoc 3.1.3 (man writer), GNU make, GitHub Actions, `cargo-deb` / `cargo-generate-rpm` / Homebrew as the packaging consumers.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-documentation-design.md` — approved by the owner on 2026-08-16 with §10.1 answered. Read it alongside this plan.

## Global Constraints

Exact values, copied from the spec and from decisions taken at approval time. Every task's requirements implicitly include this section.

- **The tagline is `like less but for Markdown`** — owner's ruling on spec §10.1, 2026-08-16. It wins in the README opener and in `Cargo.toml`'s `description`. **`demo/mdmost.toml` already carries it verbatim, so the demo needs no change**; do not touch `demo/`.
- **pandoc 3.1.3** is the version this is designed against, and it is what the repository machine has.
- **The generation command is exactly** `pandoc --standalone --to man docs/manual.md -o man/mdmost.1`.
- **`man/` is gitignored and never committed.** A file that does not exist cannot be stale, so there is **no staleness check** anywhere.
- **The manual's date comes from YAML metadata, hand-edited**, never from the build clock. **`footer` carries no version number.**
- **README target: roughly 150 lines**, and it **must contain no box-drawing characters at all**.
- **Every README link and image that points into `docs/` must be an absolute URL** — `https://github.com/oetiker/mdmost/blob/main/...` for pages, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oetiker/mdmost/main/...` for the image. `Cargo.toml` excludes `docs/**`, so a relative link has nothing to resolve against on crates.io.
- **Man section headings are ALL CAPS level-1 headings** in `docs/manual.md`. Verified with pandoc 3.1.3: `#` → `.SH`, `##` → `.SS`, and a pandoc definition list → `.TP`.
- **The demo is not touched by this work.** It has already been re-recorded; spec §10.2's note about a stale recording is itself stale and must not be acted on.
- **4-core cap on every cargo invocation** (`cargo test -j4`, `cargo build -j4`) — repository-wide rule, not specific to this plan.
- **Never read a gate's result through a pipe.** Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` bare and read the output.

## Verified facts this plan rests on

These were tested on the repository machine on 2026-08-16, not inferred. Do not re-derive them; do not doubt them without re-running the command.

| Claim | How it was checked | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pandoc turns a definition list into `.TP` | ran the writer on a probe file | confirmed |
| `#`/`##` become `.SH`/`.SS` | same probe | confirmed |
| YAML metadata order in `.TH` | same probe | `.TH "MDMOST" "1" "<date>" "<footer>" "<header>"` |
| `man --warnings` on pandoc output | `man --warnings -l probe.1` | **font warnings always: `cannot select font 'CB'`, and `'C'` once the page contains a code block** |
| the crate already ships a `LICENSE` | `cargo package --list` | confirmed |
| `man/mdmost.1` is currently tracked | `git ls-files man/` | confirmed — it must be removed from the index |

**The font warnings are pandoc's own font macros**, not defects. `CB` comes from the font-probe preamble (`.ie "\f[CB]x\f[]"x"`) in every page pandoc generates; `C` comes from `\f[C]`, which pandoc emits for every fenced code block, and appeared as soon as the manual gained one. Spec §9's acceptance criterion "renders without roff warnings" cannot be met literally. **The criterion this plan holds itself to is: no warnings other than `cannot select font 'C'` and `'CB'`.**

## File structure

| File | Status | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/manual.md` | **create** | The single source of reference truth. Authored. Also the pandoc input. |
| `man/mdmost.1` | **delete from git** | Becomes a build artifact. Still exists on disk after `make man`. |
| `Makefile` | **create** | One target, `man`. Nothing else — broader targets are out of scope. |
| `.gitignore` | modify | add `man/` |
| `Cargo.toml` | modify | `description`, and `man/**` added to `exclude` |
| `README.md` | **rewrite** | ~150 lines: sell, install, quick start, cheat sheet, links out |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | modify | new `docs` job — fails the PR when the manual stops converting |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | modify | `make man` as the first step of `build-binaries` |
| `tests/glyph_inventory.rs` | **create** | Pins the non-ASCII codepoints the renderer emits |
| `CHANGES.md` | modify | one `### Changed` entry under Unreleased |
| `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-13-documentation-design.md` | modify | status → executed |

## Task order and why

The manual must exist before anything generates from it, so Task 1 authors enough of it to generate a page equal to today's. The plumbing that removes `man/mdmost.1` from git lands in Task 2 **together with both CI changes**, so the repository is never in a state where a release run would fail for want of a man page. The glyph inventory test (Task 4) comes **before** the terminal-setup section (Task 5) because the spec requires that section's block list to be derived empirically rather than guessed — Task 4 is what derives it. The README rewrite is last of the content tasks because it can only link to sections that already exist.

### Task 1: The manual's reference half, and `make man`

Translate the existing man page into `docs/manual.md` and add the Makefile. At the end of this task, `make man` regenerates a page equivalent to the one in git today. Nothing is deleted yet, so this task is risk-free and independently reviewable.

**Files:**
- Create: `docs/manual.md`
- Create: `Makefile`
- Reference (do not modify): `man/mdmost.1`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: `docs/manual.md` with ALL-CAPS level-1 sections `NAME`, `SYNOPSIS`, `DESCRIPTION`, `OPTIONS`, `KEYS`, `ENVIRONMENT`, `FILES`, `EXIT STATUS`, `SEE ALSO`, `AUTHOR`. Later tasks insert `LINKS AND FOOTNOTES`, `SELECTING AND COPYING`, `CONFIGURATION`, `RENDERING` and `TERMINAL SETUP` **between `KEYS` and `ENVIRONMENT`**. The `Makefile` target is named `man`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the YAML front matter and the NAME/SYNOPSIS sections**

Create `docs/manual.md` starting exactly with:

```markdown
---
title: MDMOST
section: 1
header: mdmost manual
footer: mdmost
date: 2026-08-13
---

# NAME

mdmost - full-screen terminal pager for a single Markdown document

# SYNOPSIS

**mdmost** \[*OPTIONS*\] \[*FILE*\]
```

`date` is edited by hand when the manual is substantively revised; it is **not** the build date. `footer` carries no version, deliberately — a version there would couple every release to doc regeneration for no reader benefit.

Note: the previous hand-written page used `User Commands` as the `.TH` header field, which is the section-1 convention. The spec chose `mdmost manual`; follow the spec.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write DESCRIPTION**

Translate `man/mdmost.1:8-24`, then expand it with the rendering model as spec §5.2 requires:

```markdown
# DESCRIPTION

**mdmost** parses a Markdown document once and draws it as styled Unicode: tables
get real borders and negotiated column widths, fenced code is syntax-highlighted,
and Mermaid diagrams are laid out as box art rather than shown as source.

Rendering is a pure function of the document, the width, the theme and the options.
No layout decision is taken at parse time, so resizing the terminal discards the
canvas and renders again rather than patching what is on screen. That is why
everything reflows, and why the same document is dense in a wide terminal and
spaced in a narrow one.

With no *FILE*, the document is read from standard input; the keyboard is then read
from */dev/tty* so the pager stays interactive. When standard output is not a
terminal, **\-\-render\-once** is implied, so `mdmost doc.md | cat` produces plain
text rather than escape sequences.
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write OPTIONS as a pandoc definition list**

Every flag from `man/mdmost.1:25-67`, cross-checked against the README's option table at `README.md:143-155`. The README table has ten rows; the man page has twelve entries because it also documents `-h`/`--help` and `-V`/`--version`. **Keep all twelve.** Format each as:

```markdown
# OPTIONS

`--render-once`

:   Render one frame to standard output and exit. Needs no terminal. Truecolour
    goes to a terminal and plain text goes anywhere else, which is what makes it
    usable for scripting and snapshotting.

`--width N`

:   Render the whole document at this width instead of the terminal's.

`--body-width N`

:   Cap the prose body at N columns and centre it; `0` for no cap.

`--no-body-width`

:   Let the body use the full terminal width.

`--theme NAME`

:   The theme to start in.

`--icons`

:   Use Nerd Font glyphs even if none appears to be installed.

`--no-icons`

:   Use plain Unicode instead of Nerd Font glyphs, at the same display width.

`--mouse`

:   Capture the mouse: the wheel scrolls, the scrollbar drags, clicks jump in the
    contents pane, and dragging over the document copies the Markdown source
    behind it.

`--toc`

:   Start with the table-of-contents pane open.

`--config PATH`

:   Read configuration from this file instead of the default.

`--licenses`

:   Print the licences of the bundled syntax definitions and exit.

`-h`, `--help`

:   Print help and exit.

`-V`, `--version`

:   Print the version and exit.
```

There is no `--color` flag; the truecolour decision is made from whether stdout is a terminal. Say so in a paragraph after the list.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write KEYS, all 45, in the existing four groups**

Translate `man/mdmost.1:68-158` verbatim in content, using `##` for the four group names so pandoc emits `.SS`. Where the README's wording at `README.md:229-304` is better than the man page's, take the README's — spec §8 says "improvement only where the README's version is better".

The four groups and their members, from the current page:

- `## Moving` — `j`/`Down`, `k`/`Up`, `d`/`Ctrl-d`, `u`/`Ctrl-u`, `space`/`Ctrl-f`/`PgDn`, `b`/`Ctrl-b`/`PgUp`, `g`/`Home`, `G`/`End`, `%`, `Left`/`Right`
- `## Structure` — `[`, `]`, `=`/`Ctrl-g`, `Tab`, `f`, `F`, `Enter`
- `## Searching` — `/`, `?`, `n`/`Ctrl-Down`, `N`/`Ctrl-Up`, `Ctrl-r`
- `## Other` — `t`, `-`, `h`/`F1`, `Esc`, `q`, and **`S`, which the man page is missing** — it is documented at `README.md:281` and `README.md:299-304`. Adding it is a genuine gap being closed, not a translation.

Each entry as a definition list item:

```markdown
## Moving

`j`, `Down`

:   Scroll down one line.
```

After the four groups, carry over the README's notes at `README.md:283-304` as prose — counts as a prefix (`10j`, `50%`), what `Esc` unwinds, `/` filtering inside the contents pane, what the status bar shows during a search, sideways scrolling, and what `S` writes.

Also carry over `README.md:226-227`: bindings are remappable and the in-app help overlay is generated from the same live binding table, so the two cannot drift.

- [ ] **Step 5: Write ENVIRONMENT, FILES, EXIT STATUS, SEE ALSO, AUTHOR**

Translate `man/mdmost.1:159-205`. Two changes, both deliberate:

1. **FILES** currently carries a paragraph about `title_banner` and `section_numbers` (`man/mdmost.1:180-192`). That is configuration reference and belongs in `CONFIGURATION`, which Task 3 creates. **Delete it here** and leave FILES describing only the config file's location and its never-fatal parse behaviour. Task 3 must pick the content up — if Task 3 is not run, this is a regression.
2. **EXIT STATUS disagrees between the two documents.** The man page lists `0` and `1`; `README.md:157` also claims `2` for bad arguments. Verify which is true before writing:

Run: `mdmost --nonsense-flag; echo "exit=$?"` — build first with `cargo build -j4` and use `target/debug/mdmost`.
Expected: clap's default is `2`. Document all three codes if it is, and only the observed ones if it is not.

```markdown
# EXIT STATUS

`0`

:   Success, including a quit from the pager and a broken pipe.

`1`

:   The document could not be read, or the terminal could not be set up.

`2`

:   The command line could not be parsed.
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the Makefile**

Create `Makefile` with exactly this content and nothing more. **The recipe line must begin with a literal tab, not spaces.**

```makefile
# The manual is authored in docs/manual.md and converted to roff on demand.
# man/ is gitignored: a generated file that is not in version control cannot
# disagree with its source, so there is nothing to keep in step and no staleness
# gate to maintain. CI runs this same target, so there is exactly one code path.
.PHONY: man

man: man/mdmost.1

man/mdmost.1: docs/manual.md
	@mkdir -p man
	pandoc --standalone --to man docs/manual.md -o man/mdmost.1
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Generate the page and read it**

Run: `make man`
Expected: `man/mdmost.1` is written with no pandoc error.

Run: `MANWIDTH=80 man --warnings -l man/mdmost.1 > /dev/null`
Expected: exit 0, and **the only warnings are `cannot select font 'C'` / `'CB'`**. Any other warning is a defect in the manual — fix it before continuing.

Run: `grep -c '^\.TP' man/mdmost.1`
Expected: a count in the mid-fifties — twelve options, forty-five keys, two environment entries, one file, three exit codes. An implausibly low count means a definition list did not parse, usually because the `:` line is not indented by four spaces or the blank line before it is missing.

Run: `grep -n '^\.SS' man/mdmost.1`
Expected: exactly four lines — `Moving`, `Structure`, `Searching`, `Other`.

- [ ] **Step 8: Compare against the page being replaced**

Run: `MANWIDTH=80 man -l man/mdmost.1 | col -bx > /tmp/new.txt; MANWIDTH=80 man -l <(git show HEAD:man/mdmost.1) | col -bx > /tmp/old.txt; diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt`

Use the scratchpad rather than `/tmp` if the repository rules require it.

Expected: differences are **additions only** — the expanded DESCRIPTION, the `S` key, exit code `2`, and the moved `title_banner` paragraph's absence. **Nothing that was documented before may have vanished except that paragraph.** Read the diff; do not skim it.

- [ ] **Step 9: Commit**

```bash
git add docs/manual.md Makefile
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
docs: the manual is authored once, in Markdown

man/mdmost.1 was hand-written roff that duplicated the README's reference
half, and two copies of the same forty-five keys drift. docs/manual.md is
now the source, and `make man` converts it.

The translation is faithful except where it is deliberately not: the
description gains the rendering model, `S` is documented for the first
time, exit code 2 is recorded, and the title_banner paragraph leaves FILES
for the configuration section that is about to exist.

Nothing is removed from git yet. This commit only adds a second way to
produce the page that is already there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
```

### Task 2: Stop committing the man page, and teach CI to build it

Everything that changes where `man/mdmost.1` comes from, in one commit, so the repository is never in a state where a release would fail.

**Files:**
- Modify: `.gitignore`
- Modify: `Cargo.toml:13` (the `exclude` list)
- Modify: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new job)
- Modify: `.github/workflows/release.yml:127-135` (new step before "Create tarball")
- Delete from git: `man/mdmost.1`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the `man` target from Task 1.
- Produces: nothing later tasks depend on.

- [ ] **Step 1: Confirm the four consumers, so the change is made with eyes open**

Run: `grep -rn "man/mdmost.1\|man1.install" Cargo.toml Formula/mdmost.rb .github/workflows/`

Expected exactly four consumers, all reading from the working tree or from our own tarball:

| Consumer | Where it reads the page |
| --- | --- |
| deb (`Cargo.toml:113`) | working tree during `build-binaries` |
| rpm (`Cargo.toml:126`) | working tree during `build-binaries` |
| release tarball (`release.yml:143`) | working tree during `build-binaries` |
| Homebrew (`Formula/mdmost.rb:39`) | our release tarball, staged by `release.yml:143` |

All three working-tree consumers run inside the same `build-binaries` job, so **one generate step at the top of that job serves all of them**. `Formula/mdmost.rb` needs **no change** — it reads the tarball, which will still contain the page.

- [ ] **Step 2: Gitignore `man/`**

Append to `.gitignore`, which currently holds only `target/` and `*.snap.new`:

```gitignore
# Generated by `make man` from docs/manual.md. Never committed: a generated file
# under version control can disagree with its source, and then it needs a gate.
man/
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Remove the page from the index, keeping it on disk**

```bash
git rm --cached man/mdmost.1
```

`--cached` is what keeps the file on disk. Confirm both halves:

Run: `git ls-files man/`
Expected: no output.

Run: `ls man/mdmost.1`
Expected: the file is still there.

- [ ] **Step 4: Exclude `man/**` from the published crate**

Modify `Cargo.toml:13`. It currently reads:

```toml
exclude = ["docs/**", "demo/**", "tests/corpus/**", "tests/snapshots/**"]
```

Change it to:

```toml
exclude = ["docs/**", "demo/**", "tests/corpus/**", "tests/snapshots/**", "man/**"]
```

The comment above it explains the first four; extend it to say that `man/` is generated and that excluding it keeps `cargo publish` from needing `--allow-dirty`. Note that `cargo install` does not install man pages, so the page inside the `.crate` was inert bytes no user could reach.

- [ ] **Step 5: Verify the crate no longer carries it**

Run: `make man` (so the file definitely exists on disk and the test is meaningful)
Run: `cargo package --list --allow-dirty | grep -c '^man/'`
Expected: `0`. If this prints anything above zero the exclude is not matching.

Run: `cargo package --list --allow-dirty | grep -E '^(LICENSE|README.md|Cargo.toml)$'`
Expected: all three still present — the exclude must not have taken anything else with it.

- [ ] **Step 6: Add the `docs` job to CI**

Append to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after the `windows` job. It installs pandoc and runs the same `make man` a contributor runs. **Nothing consumes the output** — its job is to fail the pull request that breaks the manual, rather than letting a release discover it.

```yaml
  docs:
    name: Manual converts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Nothing consumes this page. The job exists so a manual that stops
      # converting fails the pull request that broke it, instead of surfacing
      # at release time when man/mdmost.1 is suddenly load-bearing.
      - name: Install pandoc
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pandoc

      - name: Build the man page
        run: make man
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Add the generate step to the release build**

In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, insert a step in the `build-binaries` job **after "Install Rust toolchain" (line 116-119) and before "Install cross" (line 121)**. It must run before "Create tarball" (line 136), "Create zip (Windows)" (line 148) and "Build deb and rpm" (line 160).

```yaml
      # man/ is not in git; it is generated from docs/manual.md. Three steps in
      # this job need the page — the tarball, the deb and the rpm — so it is
      # built once here, before any of them.
      - name: Build the man page
        run: |
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "macOS" ]; then
            brew install pandoc
          elif [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then
            choco install pandoc -y
          else
            sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pandoc
          fi
          make man
        shell: bash
```

**The Windows leg needs care.** `release.yml:148-158` builds a zip that copies only `README.md` and `LICENSE` — it does **not** copy the man page. So Windows does not need pandoc at all. Prefer skipping it there over installing a package that nothing uses:

```yaml
      - name: Build the man page
        if: '!matrix.windows'
        run: |
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "macOS" ]; then
            brew install pandoc
          else
            sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y pandoc
          fi
          make man
        shell: bash
```

Use the second form. Confirm the claim it rests on before you do:

Run: `sed -n '148,158p' .github/workflows/release.yml`
Expected: no `man` in the Windows zip staging. If there is one, use the first form instead.

- [ ] **Step 8: Check the workflow files still parse**

Run: `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; [yaml.safe_load(open(f)) for f in ['.github/workflows/ci.yml','.github/workflows/release.yml']]; print('both parse')"`
Expected: `both parse`.

- [ ] **Step 9: Prove the pipeline works from a clean checkout**

This is spec §9's first acceptance criterion and the one most worth actually running.

```bash
rm -rf /scratch/oetiker/claude-tmp/manual-clean-check
git clone --no-hardlinks . /scratch/oetiker/claude-tmp/manual-clean-check
cd /scratch/oetiker/claude-tmp/manual-clean-check
ls man/ 2>&1          # expected: no such file or directory
make man
ls man/mdmost.1       # expected: it exists
```

Expected: the clone has no `man/` at all, and `make man` creates it with nothing installed but pandoc. **This is the moment the whole design is either true or false.** Return to the repository afterwards.

- [ ] **Step 10: Commit**

```bash
git add .gitignore Cargo.toml .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/release.yml
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
build: the man page is generated at build time, not kept in git

A generated file under version control can disagree with its source, so it
needs a staleness gate, and the gate is a thing to maintain and a way to
fail a build for a reason no reader cares about. A file that does not
exist cannot be stale.

All four consumers keep working. The deb, the rpm and the release tarball
read the page from the working tree inside build-binaries, so one generate
step at the top of that job serves all three; Homebrew reads our tarball
and is untouched. Windows ships no man page and so skips pandoc.

man/** joins the crate's exclude list. Nothing is lost: cargo install does
not install man pages, so the page inside the .crate was bytes no user
could reach — and excluding it is what keeps cargo publish from needing
--allow-dirty against an untracked man/.

CI gains a docs job that converts the manual and throws the result away.
It exists to fail the pull request that breaks the manual rather than the
release that needed it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
```

### Task 4: `tests/glyph_inventory.rs`

Pin the non-ASCII codepoints the renderer emits, so the manual's terminal-setup section cannot silently stop matching the renderer. **This task comes before the section it protects, because the section's block list must be derived from this test's output rather than guessed.**

**What this test does NOT do, and the comment at the top of the file must say so:** it tests against no font whatsoever and cannot. It compares two things that are both inside this repository — the codepoints the renderer emits, and the inventory this file documents. It says nothing about whether any font on any machine has glyphs for them. **Checking that would mean rasterising a font and asserting something about the reader's system, which this project does not do in code and which would be wrong on the next machine.** The claim is narrow: §TERMINAL SETUP's block list cannot silently stop matching the renderer.

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/glyph_inventory.rs`
- Read: `tests/corpus/*.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `mdmost::doc::Doc`, `mdmost::render::{RenderOptions, render_document}`, `mdmost::theme::Theme`, `canvas.height()`, `canvas.row_text(row)` — the same API `tests/render_plain_text.rs:12-25` uses.
- Produces: the empirical block list Task 5 writes into the manual.

**A limitation to state in the file and to carry into Task 5:** this covers the **renderer** only. The TUI chrome — the status bar's `⌕`, the scrollbar's block elements, the `‹`/`›` cut markers — is drawn in `src/tui/` by inline literals with no central table, and is out of this test's reach. Task 5 must derive those by hand and the manual must not imply they are checked.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the collector and a deliberately empty inventory**

Create `tests/glyph_inventory.rs`:

```rust
//! The manual claims mdmost draws a particular set of Unicode blocks. This pins
//! that claim to what the renderer actually emits.
//!
//! # What this does not test
//!
//! It tests against no font whatsoever, and it cannot. It compares two things
//! that are both inside this repository: the codepoints the renderer emits, and
//! the inventory below. It says nothing about whether any font on any machine
//! has glyphs for them — checking that would mean rasterising a font and
//! asserting something about the reader's system, which is an assumption this
//! project does not make in code and which would be wrong on the next machine.
//!
//! # What it does test
//!
//! That the manual's TERMINAL SETUP block list cannot silently stop matching the
//! renderer. Add a glyph the manual does not mention and this fails, naming the
//! codepoint. It pins the *inventory*, not the appearance, so it does not
//! constrain the renderer — only the honesty of the documentation.
//!
//! # What it cannot see
//!
//! The TUI chrome. The status bar, the scrollbar and the cut markers are drawn
//! in `src/tui/` by inline literals with no central table, and nothing here
//! renders them. Those entries in the manual are maintained by hand.

use mdmost::doc::Doc;
use mdmost::render::{RenderOptions, render_document};
use mdmost::theme::Theme;
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

/// Every non-ASCII codepoint the renderer emits for one source, at one width,
/// with one set of options.
fn emitted(source: &str, width: u16, options: &RenderOptions) -> BTreeSet<char> {
    let doc = Doc::parse_auto(source);
    let canvas = render_document(&doc, width, None, &Theme::default_dark(), options);
    (0..canvas.height())
        .flat_map(|row| canvas.row_text(row).chars().collect::<Vec<_>>())
        .filter(|c| !c.is_ascii())
        .collect()
}

/// The documented inventory: every non-ASCII codepoint the renderer is allowed
/// to emit, grouped by Unicode block exactly as the manual groups them.
///
/// Adding a glyph means adding it here AND to the manual's TERMINAL SETUP
/// section. That is the whole point of this file.
const INVENTORY: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    // ("Unicode block name", "the characters from that block"),
];
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing test**

Append:

```rust
/// The seven Mermaid families. `tests/corpus/` has `diagrams.md` and
/// `pipeline.mmd` but does not exercise all seven, and a family whose glyphs are
/// never rendered is a family this inventory cannot see.
const MERMAID_FIXTURES: &[&str] = &[
    "```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B{OK?}\n  B -->|yes| C([Go])\n  B -->|no| D[(Store)]\n  subgraph S\n    C --> E((End))\n  end\n```\n",
    "```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n  participant A as Alice\n  actor B\n  A->>B: hello\n  activate B\n  B-->>A: hi\n  deactivate B\n  loop every day\n    A-xB: ping\n  end\n  Note over A,B: done\n```\n",
    "```mermaid\nclassDiagram\n  class Shape {\n    <<interface>>\n    +draw() void\n    #size int\n  }\n  Shape <|-- Circle\n  Shape *-- Point\n  Shape o-- Style\n  Circle ..> Helper\n```\n",
    "```mermaid\nerDiagram\n  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places\n  ORDER }|..|{ LINE : contains\n  CUSTOMER {\n    string name PK \"the name\"\n    int id FK\n  }\n```\n",
    "```mermaid\nstateDiagram-v2\n  [*] --> Idle\n  Idle --> Busy : work\n  state Busy {\n    [*] --> Step\n  }\n  Busy --> [*]\n```\n",
    "```mermaid\npie showData\n  title Languages\n  \"Rust\" : 70\n  \"TOML\" : 30\n```\n",
    "```mermaid\ngantt\n  title Plan\n  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD\n  section One\n  Design :done, d1, 2026-01-01, 5d\n  Build  :active, crit, after d1, 10d\n  Ship   :milestone, 2026-02-01, 0d\n```\n",
];

/// Everything the renderer is asked to draw, across the widths and option sets
/// that change which glyphs come out.
fn everything_emitted() -> BTreeSet<char> {
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();

    let corpus: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/tests/corpus"))
        .expect("tests/corpus must be readable")
        .map(|entry| entry.expect("a readable dir entry").path())
        .filter(|path| {
            matches!(path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()), Some("md" | "mmd"))
        })
        .map(|path| std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("a readable corpus file"))
        .collect();

    let sources = corpus.iter().map(String::as_str).chain(MERMAID_FIXTURES.iter().copied());

    for source in sources {
        // Both glyph sets, and both line-number settings: icons changes the
        // code-fence language icon, and nothing else in the body.
        for icons in [true, false] {
            for line_numbers in [true, false] {
                let options = RenderOptions::new(icons, line_numbers)
                    .with_title_banner(true)
                    .with_copy_button(true);
                // Narrow forces wrapping, the table gap row and the cut markers;
                // wide leaves everything dense.
                for width in [40, 80, 200] {
                    seen.extend(emitted(source, width, &options));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    seen
}

#[test]
fn every_glyph_the_renderer_emits_is_in_the_documented_inventory() {
    let documented: BTreeSet<char> = INVENTORY
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|(_, chars)| chars.chars())
        .collect();

    let undocumented: Vec<String> = everything_emitted()
        .difference(&documented)
        .map(|c| format!("U+{:04X} {c}", *c as u32))
        .collect();

    assert!(
        undocumented.is_empty(),
        "the renderer emits {} codepoint(s) the manual does not document.\n\
         Add them to INVENTORY here and to the manual's TERMINAL SETUP section:\n  {}",
        undocumented.len(),
        undocumented.join("\n  ")
    );
}
```

The new content, and the reason the owner asked for this work. Written **coverage first, font names second**: the requirement is which Unicode blocks the terminal font must cover; named fonts are examples that satisfy it, never an instruction to install a particular font.

**Files:**

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the block list from the test, not from memory**

Open `tests/glyph_inventory.rs` and transcribe the `INVENTORY` block names into a table. The manual and the test must name the same blocks in the same words, so a reader who hits the test failure can find the section it means.

```markdown
# TERMINAL SETUP

mdmost draws with characters from these Unicode blocks. Your terminal font, or
a fallback behind it, has to cover them.

| Block | What mdmost draws from it |
| --- | --- |
| Box Drawing (U+2500–U+257F) | every table border, code frame and diagram box |
| Block Elements (U+2580–U+259F) | zebra stripes, the scrollbar, gantt bars |
| Geometric Shapes (U+25A0–U+25FF) | heading marks, diagram node shapes, arrowheads |
| Arrows (U+2190–U+21FF) | Mermaid edges |
| General Punctuation (U+2000–U+206F) | em dashes, ellipses, the `‹` `›` cut markers |
| Private Use Area (U+E000–U+F8FF) | Nerd Font code-fence language icons, when icons are on |
```

Complete the table from the test's real inventory. Add a line saying the Private Use Area row applies only when icons are on, and that it is the one row a reader can opt out of.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write what goes wrong without coverage**

This is the part that earns the section. It is also exactly what a reader may have just seen on GitHub, so say so:

```markdown
## What goes wrong without it

A missing glyph is not usually a blank box. The terminal falls back to another
font, and that font's advance width need not match the base font's — so a line
made *entirely* of box characters comes out a different width from the text
lines around it, and the frame stops lining up. A table's rules overshoot its
contents; a diagram's boxes shear.

This is not a bug you can fix from inside mdmost. Every row it draws is padded
to exactly the width of the pane, measured in display columns; what the
terminal then does with those columns is the font stack's business.

If you have seen these frames misalign in a browser, that is the same fault one
layer up: GitHub strips CSS from Markdown, so the font stack there is not ours
to set either.
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the platform fixes, copy-pasteable**

```markdown
## Fixing it

**Linux (fontconfig).** Put a fallback chain in
`~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf` and run `fc-cache -f`:

    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <alias>
        <family>monospace</family>
        <prefer>
          <family>JetBrains Mono</family>
          <family>Symbols Nerd Font</family>
          <family>JuliaMono</family>
        </prefer>
      </alias>
    </fontconfig>

**macOS and Windows.** fontconfig is not in play; the terminal decides. Set the
fallback in the terminal's own font settings — iTerm2 has "Use a different font
for non-ASCII text", Windows Terminal takes a `font.fallback` list in
`settings.json`, and Kitty and WezTerm both take an explicit fallback list in
their config.
```

Use an indented code block for the XML rather than a fenced one **only if a fence causes trouble in the man output**; check with `make man`. A fenced block is preferred if it converts cleanly.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the known-good stack**

Presented as an example that satisfies the requirement, never as a requirement:

```markdown
## A stack known to work

This trio, consulted in that order, covers everything mdmost draws:

- **JetBrains Mono** — the text font.
- **Symbols Nerd Font** — the Private Use Area icons.
- **JuliaMono** — Unicode's symbol blocks: arrows, geometric shapes, dingbats,
  braille.

It is named because it is known to work, not because mdmost wants it. Any font
or chain that covers the blocks above will do.
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write the icons paragraph**

```markdown
## Icons are detected, not assumed

No terminal can be asked what font it is using. So mdmost asks fontconfig
whether an installed font covers every glyph it would draw, and uses icons only
if one does. It picks plain whenever it cannot establish that — when `fc-list`
is unavailable, when output is not going to a terminal, on `TERM=dumb` or the
Linux console, and **over SSH**, where the fonts on the machine running mdmost
say nothing about the terminal drawing the pixels.

Guessing wrong towards plain costs a little elegance; guessing wrong towards
icons fills the screen with replacement boxes. The tie does not go to the
prettier answer.

Plain and icon glyphs occupy **the same display width**, so nothing shifts and
nothing reflows either way. To decide for yourself, see `icons` under
CONFIGURATION.
```

This is condensed from `README.md:189-223`, which Task 6 deletes.

## Open questions the executor must not decide alone

1. **Definition lists do not render on GitHub.** `docs/manual.md` uses pandoc definition lists because that is what produces `.TP`, and the spec chose that deliberately (§3). But GFM has no definition lists, so on GitHub — and in mdmost itself, which renders GFM — every entry will show as a paragraph followed by a paragraph starting with `:`. **The manual's stated audience is "someone using it, on the web", so this is a real conflict the spec did not address.** Build Task 1, then show the owner the rendered result at `https://github.com/oetiker/mdmost/blob/<branch>/docs/manual.md` and ask. The fallback, if it reads badly, is a bulleted list of `**term** — description`, which costs the `.TP` shape and gives `.IP` instead. **Do not switch unilaterally.**
2. **The `.TH` header field** changes from `User Commands` to `mdmost manual`. `User Commands` is the section-1 convention. The spec chose otherwise; it is trivially reversible in the front matter.
3. **The chrome glyphs are documented by hand.** `tests/glyph_inventory.rs` covers the renderer only. If the manual's block list should be enforced for the status bar and scrollbar too, that needs a way to render the TUI headlessly, which does not exist and is not in this spec.

## Self-review

**Spec coverage.** §2 the three artifacts → Tasks 1, 2, 6. §3 generation, metadata, Makefile, both CI sites → Tasks 1 and 2. §4 the README's ten parts, absolute links → Task 6. §5 the manual's eleven sections → Tasks 1, 3, 5. §6 terminal setup → Task 5. §7 the glyph test → Task 4. §8 non-goals → honoured; `demo/` untouched, no Pages site, no `mdmost(5)`, no font installation, translation-first. §9 acceptance → Task 7 Step 4, with the two unrunnable criteria named rather than dropped. §10.1 tagline → Task 6 Step 3; §10.2 → already resolved, recorded in Task 7 Step 2.

**Type consistency.** `RenderOptions::new(icons, line_numbers)` plus `.with_title_banner(bool)` and `.with_copy_button(bool)` match `src/render/mod.rs:113-148`. `Doc::parse_auto`, `render_document(&doc, width, None, &theme, &options)`, `canvas.height()`, `canvas.row_text(row)` match `tests/render_plain_text.rs:12-25`. The Makefile target is `man` everywhere.

**Known soft spot.** Task 4 Step 4's block table is a source-level survey, not the test's output, and the plan says so twice and tells the executor to use the real output. That is the one place a careless executor could write a plausible-but-wrong list.
